column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/pleme-iac.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS FILE IS. pleme-iac is a TIER-2 COMPOSER: five sibling jobs, no
# `needs:` edges between them, each gated by a single equality on the one input
# the workflow takes. Every arm is a pure router — it does no work itself, it
# selects one leaf reusable and hands off. `inputs.target` is therefore the ONLY
# context path any condition here reads, which is why every case below declares
# exactly that one key and nothing else.
# WHAT IT PINS, and why a router of all things needs pinning:
#  1. EACH ARM IS REACHABLE. Rows 1-5 give one row per arm. A typo in any `if:`
#     string, or a job renamed without its condition following, turns that arm
#     into a job that can never select — and a router with a dead arm looks
#     exactly like a router that works, because the other four still fire. The
#     linter calls that NEVER; these five rows are what make it callable.
#  2. AN UNROUTABLE TARGET SELECTS NOTHING, AND THAT IS ALL IT DOES. Rows 6-7
#     are the boundary. This composer has NO catch-all arm and no validation job
#     of its own: hand it a name it does not know and all five conditions are
#     simply false, every job skips, and the workflow reports SUCCESS having
#     published nothing. All five leaves here publish or release something (a
#     Crossplane function, a Crossplane provider, a Pulumi provider, a Steampipe
#     plugin, a Terraform provider), so "no arm selected" is precisely the
#     green-tick-over-nothing shape this linter exists for, one composition level
#     up from the graphql-synthesizer run that motivated it.
#     That is DELIBERATE and stays deliberate: the guard lives in the caller.
#     pleme.yml's `validate` job greps this very file for the literal
#     `inputs.target == '<t>'` and fails the run before dispatching. But
#     pleme-iac's own header invites direct calls ("calling it directly also
#     works and simply spends one fewer chain level"), and a direct caller
#     bypasses `validate` entirely. Rows 6-7 write that down so the next reader
#     inherits the fact instead of rediscovering it from a silent run. If a
#     catch-all/fail-loud arm is ever added here, these two rows are the ones
#     that must change — they are the intent, not an accident of the current
#     shape.
# Row 6 uses a REAL reusable from a different family (cargo-auto-release, a
# `rust` leaf) rather than an invented string: mis-routing a valid target into
# the wrong family composer is the realistic form of this mistake, not a typo
# nobody would type. Row 7 is the empty value, which models "the caller computed
# a target and produced nothing" — a distinct state from any named value, and
# the one a catch-all written as an `else` would most likely get wrong.
# No condition here calls always()/success()/failure()/cancelled(), and none uses
# contains()/startsWith()/fromJSON()/hashFiles(), so nothing in this workflow is
# unassertable.
# ── 1-5: one row per arm. Each proves its own arm reachable AND proves the
#         other four are gated off by the same value, which is what makes the
#         dispatch exclusive rather than merely functional.
crossplane-function
crossplane-provider
pulumi-provider
steampipe-plugin
terraform-provider
# ── 6: a valid target of ANOTHER family. Nothing publishes. Intended: the caller
#       (pleme.yml validate) is what rejects this; called directly, it is a
#       silent no-op by design.
foreign-family-target-publishes-nothing
# ── 7: the caller resolved a target and produced nothing. Distinct from any
#       named value; also nothing publishes.
empty-target-publishes-nothing
